adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:1 — deleteCache mutation has no rate limiting, so repeated calls can be used to force expensive cache rebuilds on every subsequent availability lookup (self-inflicted cache-thrashing DoS)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authenticated `deleteCache` mutation (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx`) whose handler (`deleteCache.handler.ts`) performs an unthrottled `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` after only checking the credential belongs to the user. The diff shows no rate limiting or other abuse controls around repeated calls, so a user could repeatedly clear their cache and negate caching benefits (cache-thrashing) and increase downstream workload. This is a real, diff-grounded operational/security-hardening concern, but not a strictly verifiable correctness defect by itself from the diff alone (no proof of “expensive rebuild” path here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:29 — deleteMany result (count of deleted rows) is discarded and handler always returns { success: true }, so the "cache deleted successfully" toast fires even when zero rows were deleted, giving misleading feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` but ignores the returned `{ count }` and always returns `{ success: true }`. On the client (`CredentialActionsDropdown`), any successful mutation triggers the "cache_deleted_successfully" toast. If there were zero rows to delete (e.g., cache already empty/expired), the user still sees a deletion-success message. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/feedback edge case, but the delete operation is still idempotently successful, so it’s not a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:23 — Throws a plain `Error` instead of `TRPCError`, so tRPC serializes it as an untyped INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, losing the "not found/access denied" semantics and breaking client error-code handling

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler checks ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst(...)` and on failure does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. Since this is invoked from a tRPC mutation (`deleteCache` in `_router.tsx`), throwing a plain `Error` will be treated as an internal/untyped server error rather than a semantic `TRPCError` (e.g., NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN), breaking client-side error-code handling for this explicit “not found/access denied” case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:8 — DEFAULT NOW()` backfills existing CalendarCache rows with the migration-run timestamp rather than their true last-write time, so the new "Last updated" UI will falsely show all pre-existing cache entries as just refreshed

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql) and the Prisma model sets `@default(now()) @updatedAt`. For pre-existing `CalendarCache` rows, the only value they will get is the migration execution timestamp (Postgres will backfill the default on existing rows), not the real last modification time. The new UI surfaces this via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `_max.updatedAt` and displays it as “Last updated” (CredentialActionsDropdown), so legacy cache entries will misleadingly appear freshly updated at migration time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:86 — Uses hardcoded Tailwind colors (text-gray-900/text-gray-500, dark:text-white) instead of design-system tokens like text-emphasis/text-subtle already used elsewhere in this same diff (SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx), causing visual inconsistency and duplicated theming logic

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, the cache status text uses hardcoded Tailwind palette classes (`text-gray-900`, `text-gray-500`, `dark:text-white`) rather than design-system semantic tokens. This is directly visible in the new component (around the cache status block inside `DropdownMenuItem`) and can lead to theming/visual inconsistency versus other parts of the UI that rely on tokenized classes (as the finding notes). This is not a functional defect but is a concrete, diff-grounded UI/theming consistency issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:1 — Component conflates two unrelated responsibilities (cache management + credential disconnect) via a loosely related prop set (credentialId, integrationType, cacheUpdatedAt, delegationCredentialId, disableConnectionModification), suggesting it should be split into a cache-actions component and a disconnect component composed together

adjudication.rationale: The new `CredentialActionsDropdown` clearly bundles two distinct action flows in one component: (1) cache management for Google Calendar (`deleteCacheMutation`, `hasCache`, cache status UI/strings, `viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) and (2) credential disconnect for any integration (`disconnectMutation`, `canDisconnect`, `viewer.credentials.delete`). This is driven by a mixed prop set (`integrationType`, `cacheUpdatedAt` vs `delegationCredentialId`, `disableConnectionModification`) and results in conditional UI composition inside a single dropdown. That’s not a correctness defect, but it is a concrete architecture/scope concern introduced by this diff and is actionable (could be split into separate composed components).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:22 — Throws a plain `Error` instead of `TRPCError({code:"NOT_FOUND"})`, so a missing/unauthorized credential surfaces as an unhandled 500 (INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) instead of a proper 404/403 client-visible error

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler checks ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` and if not found it does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC, throwing a plain `Error` is typically mapped to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) rather than a client-meaningful `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN` via `TRPCError`, so missing/unauthorized credentials will surface as a 500 instead of an appropriate status/code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1023 — SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId` is awaited with no try/catch inside watchCalendar/cache-refresh flow, so a DB failure here throws after cache data was already fetched/set, aborting the whole watch flow instead of degrading gracefully

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` (after fetching availability and writing cache). There is no local error handling around this new DB write, so any prisma failure would propagate and cause the enclosing calendar watch/refresh method to throw even though the cache work already completed. The claim that this should “degrade gracefully” is an architectural/robustness concern rather than a definitively verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx:29 — deleteCache input schema `z.object({ credentialId: z.number() })` does not restrict to a positive integer, allowing negative/float/NaN values to reach the Prisma query (harmless due to ownership filter but is a defense-in-depth gap)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the `deleteCache` TRPC mutation with input validation `z.object({ credentialId: z.number() })` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx). This indeed does not enforce an integer/positive constraint (e.g., `z.number().int().positive()`), so negative or non-integer numeric values could pass Zod and reach `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }})` in `deleteCache.handler.ts`. That’s a legitimate defense-in-depth/input-hardening issue grounded in the added code, though not necessarily a functional defect for normal callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:14 — New deleteCache mutation, including its ownership-check branch (credential not found/not owned) that throws an error, has no unit test covering authorized vs unauthorized deletion

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `deleteCache` mutation and handler (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx` and `deleteCache.handler.ts`). The handler contains nontrivial authorization/ownership logic (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }})` and `if (!credential) throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`) plus a destructive operation (`prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany`). This change is significant enough that tests differentiating authorized vs unauthorized deletion would be valuable, and the diff does not add any such tests alongside the new logic.
